title: Communicating The Uncertainty Of Extraterrestrial Life: How The News Media Portrayed The Contested Phosphine Detection On Venus

content:
[International Journal of Astrobiology]. The contested 2020 report of phosphine in Venus’s atmosphere triggered one of the most prominent recent debates in astrobiology, raising the possibility of extraterrestrial life while exposing deep scientific uncertainty.

This study examines how English-language news media communicated this uncertainty over time and across news outlet types. Drawing on a standardized content analysis of news coverage published between September 2020 and June 2025, we trace shifts in uncertainty framing across four periods of the scientific debate. Findings show that media coverage was closely aligned to the scientific agenda.

However, media reports – particularly during the initial discovery period – often expressed greater certainty about both phosphine and extraterrestrial life than was apparent in exemplary scientific publications. Consensus uncertainty was the most prominent uncertainty frame, accurately reflecting expert disagreement while posing potential challenges for public trust.

Media types differed markedly, with mass-market media exhibiting more sensational framing and specialist science outlets adopting greater epistemic caution. Notably, clickbaiting strategies were relatively rare across the sample. Together, the findings show how media coverage selectively communicates and contextualizes uncertainty in reporting on frontier science.
